activities.label: Overview map
activities.title: Europe before the war
activities.body: Read the overview and build the big picture.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions formed rival blocs and made a local crisis more dangerous.

activities.label: Closed-note recall
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Answer from memory in one or two sentences.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination set off the July Crisis, which led to mobilization and then declarations of war as alliances pulled more countries in.
activities.feedback: A complete answer shows the spark, the crisis, and the move to wider war in order.

activities.label: Fix the sequence
activities.title: Check the war sequence
activities.body: Revise your answer with the missing link made explicit.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination directly caused war without an intervening crisis and mobilization step.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination did not instantly cause general war; the July Crisis, mobilization, and alliance commitments came between the shooting and the declarations of war.
activities.feedback: Repair the gap by naming the steps between the assassination and war.

activities.label: Timeline recall
activities.title: WWI start to finish
activities.body: Give the timeline from memory in order.
activities.correctAnswer: 1914 war begins, 1917 the United States enters, 1918 the armistice ends the fighting.
activities.feedback: A complete answer puts the main milestones in the correct order.

activities.label: Recognition check
activities.title: Order the major milestones
activities.body: Choose the best order for the war’s main milestones.
choices: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice
1917 armistice, 1914 United States enters, 1918 war begins
1918 war begins, 1914 armistice, 1917 United States enters
1914 armistice, 1917 war begins, 1918 United States enters
activities.correctAnswer: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice
activities.feedback: The correct chronology runs from outbreak to U.S. entry to the armistice.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Explain an idea in plain language, compare it with an accurate source, repair the gaps, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Connecting steps, causes, and prior knowledge can expose shallow understanding and build a more useful mental model.
how: Study one concise explanation or example.
Close it and explain the idea in your own words.
Name the cause, relationship, or reason behind each important step.
Compare with the source, repair the explanation, then teach it back again without copying.
methodBriefing.completion: The explanation accurately includes the central relationship and at least one supporting reason or example.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: Rival blocs before war
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided powers into rival blocs before 1914.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: Rival blocs before war
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances and tensions shape the balance of power before 1914?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided powers into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances did not prevent war; they increased the risk of wider conflict.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum, then Serbia's reply, then declarations of war.
Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 begins with war in 1914 and ends with the armistice in 1918.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: What sequence followed the Sarajevo assassination before general war began?
activities.concept: Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum, then Serbia's reply, then
activities.correctAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, Serbia replied, and declarations of war followed.
activities.feedback: Keep the order clear: assassination, ultimatum, reply, then war declarations.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: War years chronology
activities.body: What is the basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 for the war's start and end?
activities.concept: Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 begins with war in 1914 and ends with the armistice in 1918.
activities.correctAnswer: The war began in 1914 and ended with the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: Use the start and end years as the main chronology, not later settlement dates.

activities.label: Repair
activities.title: Repair the first explanation
activities.body: Compare the first explanation with this verified reference: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread. Correct the exposed relationship in your own words without copying the reference.
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided powers into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances did not prevent war; they increased the risk of wider conflict.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Explain the corrected relationship again
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances and tensions shape the balance of power before 1914? Explain it again after the repair without copying the model or reference answer.
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided powers into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances did not prevent war; they increased the risk of wider conflict.

activities.label: Recall check
activities.title: War begins in which year
activities.body: Which year marks the start of the basic chronology from 1914 to 1918?
activities.concept: Recognition transfer: Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 begins with war in 1914 and ends with the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: 1914 is the war's starting year in this chronology.
